verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text: Rain finds the same crack in the sidewalk every spring—

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the crack does not ask forgiveness, only water,
and water gives itself without a name.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep no ledger of what the river takes—
only my thirst, only this cracked-open cup.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The cup remembers the hand that shaped it—
a wet thumb turning silence into shape.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light burning all night—
moths arrive like small unanswered questions.
